name: Tapform
summary: No-code builder for multi-step lead capture forms, quizzes and popups that you embed on any website, with lead notifications, tracking pixels and CRM integrations; a small free plan and an unlimited plan for agencies and growing sites.
best_for: small businesses, solo marketers and agencies that want multi-step lead capture forms on any website for a few dollars a month, without a developer
skip_if: you need more than a form, such as call tracking, a full CRM or detailed attribution; or your site already has a form builder that captures and routes leads well enough
honest_knock: The free plan stops at 5 leads a month on one form, so it is a trial in all but name. The yearly price on the pricing page does not add up: it shows $29.99 'per month, billed yearly' against $4.99 a month on monthly billing. And according to the terms the trial turns into a paid plan unless you cancel, while the pricing page suggests you simply drop back to Free.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-18 in a browser on tapform.com/pricing in the monthly and yearly view; the page shows $ without naming a currency) Two plans. Free is $0.00 a month: 5 leads a month, 1 form, 1 workspace, 1 user, 100 MB of storage, 15+ templates, the embed code and email lead notifications. Unlimited is $4.99 a month billed monthly: unlimited leads, forms, workspaces, team members, domains and storage. Switching the toggle to Yearly, which carries a 'Save 50%' badge, shows Unlimited as $29.99 'per month, billed yearly' next to a struck-through $4.99; that does not add up as a saving and the page gives no yearly invoice total, so we do not quote a yearly price. New accounts get a 14-day trial with full access to the plan's features. The pricing page says that when it ends you choose a plan or continue on Free; the terms say you are charged automatically unless you cancel. The terms allow a refund request within 14 calendar days of the first subscription purchase, processed through LemonSqueezy.

compare_with.name: Deftform
compare_with.why: Deftform is in our dossiers too and is also a no-code form builder sold cheaply: when we read it on 14 October 2026 it was €4 per form pre-paid in packs of five, €25 a month for Complete with unlimited forms, or €189 once for a lifetime licence, all excluding VAT. Tapform costs less per month at $4.99 for Unlimited and is built around lead capture, with multi-step forms, popups and tracking pixels for ad platforms on its feature list. Deftform is the more general form tool and the one with a one-off price.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 6 November 2026 on the free trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We built one lead form, published it and sent one fictional test lead through it. We did not export the lead and did not open checkout.
findings: The plan page opens in the monthly view: Free at $0.00 with 5 leads a month and Unlimited at $4.99 a month. That matches our read of 18 October. The Free button did not respond, so we used Skip. No card was asked for.

The welcome screen says 'Your free trial of Tapform starts today' and shows decorative cards reading 'Payment successful'. Nothing was paid. Inside the app, a pop-up then says 'You are on free plan' and a banner repeats it, which does not fit a trial that had just started.
A pop-up offering a free call with a sales person appeared twice during the session.

The default form comes with a consent text under it. It says Tapform and its providers may contact you by text or call, some of it automated, once the form is submitted. Check that wording before you put the form on your own site.

Our title and description with the accent in 'Zoë', the quotation marks and the dash were saved and shown correctly. The published form carries a 'Powered by tapform' badge, and its public address is built from the account holder's full name.

The address block took only five-digit US-style ZIP codes. The field is numeric, so the Dutch postcode '3011 AB' was cut to '3011' and then refused with 'Zip must be 5 digit number!', although the country was set to the Netherlands. We typed '30110' to get past it. The lead arrived with that value.

After the submit, the thank-you screen carries an advert, 'Create your Tapform'. The lead list showed our lead and a demo lead that was already there. The counter read 'Leads collected 1/5', so the demo lead does not count.
The lead detail kept the accent and the quotation marks. We could not confirm from the text view that the line break in the notes field survived.
not_tested: Export and re-import: there is an 'Export all' button on the lead list, but we did not click it, so no file was opened
The second fictional record: we sent one lead only
Checkout, tax and the final price
Support, team roles, API access, invitations, downgrade and cancellation
How many screens sign-up took in full; Daan created the account before we started counting
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
